os-net-extract.title: Data extraction
os-net-extract.summary: Read fields such as a title, a price or an image from a web page or a JSON answer, with the rules written in configuration, not in code.

gives.1: Describe a site once, as selectors and JSON paths with fallbacks, and read the same fields from any of its pages.
gives.2: Fetch pages safely: private addresses are refused, the body has a size limit, and a bad answer becomes a state, not an exception.
gives.3: The HTML engine sits behind an interface, so the parser can change without touching the code that uses it.

sample.quick: Read the title of a page by its host

providers.title: Providers and fields
providers.summary: Write what to read from each site as configuration.

1.title: Rules in config
1.text: Each site is described by an `ExtractProvider`, not by code.

2.title: Fields
2.text: Each `ExtractField` says where to read a value from.

3.title: Simple setup
3.text: `AddOSExtract` registers one safe HTTP client per provider.

4.title: Always safe
4.text: Private addresses are refused and big pages are not read.

1.title: Describing a source
1.text:
An `ExtractProvider` describes one source. `Name` is its name and `Host` is the host it serves. `BaseUrl` is optional.

`Format` is `Html` or `Json`. `Timeout` is in seconds. `Priority` sets the order and `Fields` is the list of fields.

2.title: Fields
2.text:
An `ExtractField` has a `Name` and the places to look.

For HTML, `Selectors` are tried in order. An `Attribute` (or several in `Attributes`) is read instead of the text. `Index` picks the n-th match and `Absolute` turns a relative link into a full one.

For JSON, `Paths` are tried in order. When the JSON sits inside a page, add an optional `Script` selector.

3.title: Setup and safety
3.text:
`AddOSExtract` takes an `ExtractConfig` or an `IConfiguration` section named `os-extract`. It registers one safe HTTP client per provider and the factory. Calling it again merges the new providers and throws when a name already exists.

Every client is in safe mode, so private addresses are refused. A page over `MaxBytes` (5 MiB by default) is not read either.

config.title: Describe a provider in JSON
config.note: The same names work in a config file under os-extract. Fields tried in order stop at the first selector that matches.

merge.title: Register providers in more than one place
merge.note: A repeated provider name throws an InvalidOperationException.

type.ExtractConfig: The user agent, the body size cap and the list of providers.
type.ExtractProvider: One source of data: where it lives, its format and its fields.
type.ExtractField: One value to read, and where to look for it.
type.ExtractFormat: Whether a provider's answer is HTML or JSON.

ExtractConfig.Probe: The name of the built-in client used for hosts that have no provider.
ExtractConfig.UserAgent: The User-Agent header sent by every client.
ExtractConfig.MaxBytes: The largest page that is read, 5 MiB by default.

ExtractProvider.Name: Unique name. It is also the name of the HTTP client.
ExtractProvider.Host: The host this provider serves, used to find it from a link.
ExtractProvider.BaseUrl: The address that relative links are added to.
ExtractProvider.Priority: Lower numbers come first in the factory's list.
ExtractProvider.MaxParallel: How many requests of SendBulkAsync run at the same time. 4 by default.

ExtractField.Name: The key of the value in the result.
ExtractField.Attribute: The attribute to read instead of the text.
ExtractField.Attributes: More attributes to try after Attribute.
ExtractField.Index: Which match to take, starting from 0.
ExtractField.Absolute: Turn a relative link into a full one, using the page address.
ExtractField.Script: A selector for the element that holds the JSON, when it is inside a page.

html.title: Reading HTML
html.summary: Read text and attributes from a page with CSS selectors.

1.title: HTML to a doc
1.text: The engine parses HTML into an `IExtractDoc`.

2.title: Read a field
2.text: `ExtractEx.Read` tries each selector in order and returns the first match.

3.title: Missing field
3.text: A field with no match gives `NotFound` with the code `extract.miss`.

4.title: No scripts run
4.text: It doesn't run scripts or load other files.

1.title: Reading one field
1.text:
The engine parses HTML into an `IExtractDoc`, and `ExtractEx.Read` applies one `ExtractField` to it. It tries each selector in order and reads the text or the attribute. It returns the first match as an `OSResult<ExtractValue>`.

A field with no match gives a `NotFound` result. Its `Data` is a miss, with the code `extract.miss`.

2.title: Reading many fields
2.text:
`ReadAll` reads a list of fields into a dictionary and skips the ones that are missing.

`Text`, `Attribute`, `TextWithFallback`, `AttributeWithFallback` and `Texts` are the same helpers one step lower, for code that doesn't use a provider.

3.title: The engine behind it
3.text:
The parser is AngleSharp, but it is hidden behind `IExtractEngine` and `IExtractDoc`. Ask the container for `IExtractEngine` and call `Parse`.

It doesn't run scripts or load other files.

read.title: Read a text and a link
read.note: Absolute turns the relative link into a full address using the page address you pass.

fallback.title: Try several selectors
fallback.note: The selector that matched is kept in the value.

texts.title: Read a list and pick one item
texts.note: Index starts from 0, so 1 is the second item.

miss.title: Handle a field that is not on the page
miss.note: A missing field is a NotFound result with a code, not an exception.

type.ExtractEx: Helpers to read fields from HTML and JSON.
type.ExtractValue: A value that was read, or a miss, with the selector or path that was used.
type.IExtractDoc: A parsed page that can be queried.

ExtractEx.Read: Reads one field, trying its selectors in order.
ExtractEx.ReadAll: Reads many fields into a dictionary, skipping the missing ones.
ExtractEx.Text: Text of the first element that matches.
ExtractEx.Attribute: An attribute of the first element that matches.
ExtractEx.TextWithFallback: Text from the first selector that matches.
ExtractEx.AttributeWithFallback: An attribute from the first selector that matches.
ExtractEx.Texts: The text of every element that matches.
ExtractEx.AddOSExtract: Registers providers, one safe HTTP client for each, the engine and the factory.
ExtractEx.ReadJson: Reads one field from a JSON element, trying its paths in order.
ExtractEx.Navigate: Walks one path and returns the JSON element, or NotFound.
ExtractEx.FromScriptTag: Returns the text of a script tag, such as application/ld+json.
ExtractEx.FromJson: Reads a JSON body into a type, with the safe defaults of OS.IO.
ExtractEx.FromHeader: Reads a header value from a dictionary.

ExtractValue.Selector: The selector or path that produced the value.

IExtractDoc.Attr: An attribute of the matching element.
IExtractDoc.Texts: The text of all matching elements.

IExtractEngine.Parse: Parses HTML. Empty text gives an Invalid result.

json.title: Reading JSON
json.summary: Read values from a JSON answer, or from JSON inside a page, with simple paths.

1.title: Simple paths
1.text: A path is names separated by dots, with an index in brackets for arrays.

2.title: In order
2.text: `ExtractEx.ReadJson` tries the paths and returns the first value that is not null.

3.title: JSON inside a page
3.text: `FromScriptTag` returns the text of a script tag.

4.title: Bad JSON
4.text: Invalid JSON gives the code `extract.json.invalid` and the state `Refused`.

1.title: Paths and reading
1.text:
A path is a list of names separated by dots, with an index in brackets for arrays, such as `data.items[1].price`.

`ExtractEx.ReadJson` tries the `Paths` of a field in order. It returns the first value that is not null, as text. Numbers and booleans come back as their JSON text.

`Navigate` does the walking for one path and returns the element. It returns `NotFound` when a name or an index doesn't exist.

2.title: JSON inside a page
2.text:
Many pages carry their data in a script tag, such as `application/ld+json`. `FromScriptTag` returns that text.

In a provider, the field's `Script` selector does the same before the paths are read.

3.title: Other helpers and errors
3.text:
`FromJson<T>` reads a whole body into a type with the safe defaults of OS.IO. `FromHeader` reads a value from a dictionary of headers.

Bad JSON gives the code `extract.json.invalid` and the state `Refused`.

path.title: Read values by path
path.note: The second field falls back to the next path when the first one is missing.

script-tag.title: Read JSON that sits inside a page
script-tag.note: Prices in JSON are often strings; the value is returned as text.

service.title: Fetching and results
service.summary: Find a provider, fetch a page and get the fields with the state of the fetch.

1.title: Find a provider
1.text: `IExtractFactory` finds a provider by name or by host.

2.title: Unknown host
2.text: A host nobody configured gets a field-less probe service.

3.title: Result with state
3.text: `ExtractResult` gives the fields with the `State` and the HTTP status.

4.title: A state, not an error
4.text: A page that can't be read is a state, not an exception.

1.title: Finding a service
1.text:
`IExtractFactory` finds a provider by name or by host and gives an `IExtractService` for it.

`GetServiceByHost` falls back to a field-less probe service for a host nobody configured. That service fetches the page and reports the state without reading fields.

2.title: Request and result
2.text:
`SendAsync` takes an `ExtractRequest` with the `Url`. Add the optional `Html` when you already have the page.

It returns an `ExtractResult` with the fields, the `State`, the HTTP `Status` and the `FinalUrl` after redirects. The `State` is one of: `Fetched`, `Missing` for 404, `Refused` for any other status, a wrong media type or a body over the limit, and `Unreachable` for network problems.

3.title: State and bulk sending
3.text:
A page that can't be read is a state, not an exception. The `OSResult` is `Ok` as long as the fetch itself finished.

`Code` explains the state, for example `extract.status` or `extract.no-fields`. `SendBulkAsync` sends a list of requests one after another and returns one result for each.

send.title: Fetch a page and read its fields
send.note: Check State before the fields; a missing page is a state, not an error.

bulk.title: Fetch many pages
bulk.note: The results come back in the order of the requests.

by-host.title: Find the provider from a link
by-host.note: With Html set, nothing is fetched; the same fields are read from the page you give.

type.IExtractFactory: Finds providers and builds services for them.
type.IExtractService: Fetches and reads pages for one provider.
type.ExtractService: The default service for HTML and JSON providers.
type.ExtractRequest: What to fetch: the provider, the address and, optionally, the page itself.
type.ExtractResult: The fields that were read and the state of the fetch.

IExtractFactory.GetProviderByHost: Finds a provider by the host it serves.
IExtractFactory.GetService: Builds the service of a provider.
IExtractFactory.GetServiceByHost: Builds the service for a host, or the probe service when no provider matches.

IExtractService.SendAsync: Fetches one page and reads its fields.
IExtractService.SendBulkAsync: Does the same for a list of requests.

ExtractRequest.Html: The page itself, when you already have it. Nothing is fetched then.

ExtractResult.Fields: The values that were read, by field name.
ExtractResult.State: Pending, Fetched, Missing, Refused or Unreachable.
ExtractResult.Status: The HTTP status, or 0 if there was none.
ExtractResult.IsRedirected: True when the final address differs from the asked one.
ExtractResult.Code: Why the state is what it is.
ExtractResult.Field: The value of a field, or empty text.
ExtractResult.Has: True when the field has a value.

ExtractCodes.ProviderNotFound: No provider has that name or host.
ExtractCodes.Unreachable: The server could not be reached.
ExtractCodes.Refused: The address, the media type or the size was refused.
ExtractCodes.Status: The server answered with a status other than 2xx.
ExtractCodes.NoFields: The page was read but no field matched.
ExtractCodes.NoRequests: The list of requests is empty.
ExtractCodes.Miss: The selector or path matched nothing.
